policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 8:1 ends at "in Christ Jesus." with no rendering of "who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit"; the RP expansion r01 would have to appear in English and does not.
ASV reads "made me free", the first-person με of r01, not the second-person σε of the base.
The unit is only the article before Ἰησοῦν; ASV "raised up Jesus from the dead" renders the proper name identically whether the article stands or is omitted, and no note is mapped here.
ASV "he that raised up Christ Jesus from the dead" renders Ἰησοῦν, which only the base reading contains; r01 and r02 have Χριστὸν alone.

ASV "through his Spirit that dwelleth in you" is the genitive διὰ τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος of r01; the mapped textual note "Many ancient authorities read because of" records the accusative base reading as the rejected alternative.
All three readings are the same three words in different order; ASV "these are sons of God" fixes English word order independently and cannot distinguish them.
ἐφ᾽ and ἐπ᾽ are orthographic variants of one preposition; ASV "in hope" is the same either way, and the sole note here is classed alternative_rendering.
ASV renders both intensives — "but ourselves also" for καὶ αὐτοὶ before the participle and "even we ourselves" after it; the NIV omission r01 would leave only one.
ἡμεῖς καὶ and καὶ ἡμεῖς differ only in the order of pronoun and conjunction; ASV "even we ourselves groan within ourselves" renders both words and settles neither order.

ASV text reads "for who hopeth for that which he seeth?" — the personal τίς as subject; the mapped textual note "Many ancient authorities read for what a man seeth, why doth he yet hope for?" records τί / τί καί as the alternative the ASV did not print.
ASV "helpeth our infirmity" is singular, the base τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ; the RP plural ταῖς ἀσθενείαις would give "infirmities".
The aorist subjunctive προσευξώμεθα and the future προσευξόμεθα alike underlie ASV's "we know not how to pray as we ought".
ASV "maketh intercession for us" can render the ὑπερ- of ὑπερεντυγχάνει alone as well as an explicit ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν; no italics or note marks the pronoun as added.

ASV text has "all things work together for good" with πάντα as subject and no expressed ὁ θεός; the mapped note "Some ancient authorities read God worketh all things with them for good" records r01 as the rejected reading.
κατακρινῶν and κατακρίνων differ only by accent; ASV's timeless relative clause "who is he that condemneth?" renders either participle, and the verse's only note is classed alternative_rendering.
ASV "It is Christ Jesus that died" renders Ἰησοῦς alongside Χριστός; the base has Χριστός alone.
ASV "yea rather" renders μᾶλλον δὲ as a unit; an added ascensive καί would be absorbed in the same English phrase, so the presence of r01's καί is not visible.
ASV "that was raised from the dead" renders ἐκ νεκρῶν, which only r01 supplies; the base has ἐγερθείς unqualified.
ASV "who also maketh intercession for us" renders καί with "also"; the WH omission r01 would leave no word for it.
ASV lists "things present, nor things to come, nor powers" — the base order ἐνεστῶτα / μέλλοντα / δυνάμεις; RP's r01 puts δυνάμεις first.
